chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when it was the last ten [days], would seclude himself in the mosque, and a dome made of hair was set up for him, and he would roll up his apron and fold his bed. And some of them said, 'And he would isolate himself from the women.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for isolating himself from the women, no [he did not do so].'
ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad isolate himself from his wives during I'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s rigorous devotion during the final ten days of Ramadan, marked by setting up a tent in the mosque and simplifying his living arrangements. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies a specific juristic detail, noting that while the Prophet intensified his worship, he did not withdraw from his wives, distinguishing between spiritual seclusion and marital separation. This distinction is significant in Shia fiqh for understanding the proper conduct of those performing I'tikaf regarding their family obligations.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, whenever it was the last ten (days of the Month of Ramazan), secluded in the Masjid, and a dome made of animal hair was set up for him<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> tightened his<sup>saww</sup> apron, and folded up his<sup>saww</sup> bed’. And one of them said, ‘And he<sup>saww</sup> isolated from the women’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for isolating from the women, so no (he<sup>saww</sup> did not do so)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from af-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, in the last ten days of the month of Ramadan would retire in Masjid in seclusion for Ttikaf with a tent made of animals’ wool pitched for him. He (the Messenger of Allah) would secure his loincloth and fold up his bed (reduced sleeping). Certain others have said that he (the Messenger of Allah) stayed away from women; but Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Isolation from women was not true.’”
